chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid - may God have Mercy upon him - narrated that Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar quoted on the authority of Yaqoob ibn Yazid, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr that Muawiyah ibn Wahab said:

Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saw me carrying some green vegetables in Medina. He said, ‘It is not good for a dignified man to carry lowly things since the people will then dare to disrespect him.’

key_terms.أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abdullah (Imam al-Sadiq, peace be upon him)
key_terms.السَّرِيِّ: the dignified / the man of status

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic perspective on maintaining dignity and avoiding disrespect through daily actions?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Khisal*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) advises the narrator against carrying humble produce, linking physical demeanor to social perception and the prevention of disrespect (*istijra’*). This reflects the Shia emphasis on *hay’a* (dignified bearing) as a means of preserving one's status and authority in society, ensuring that outward actions align with inner nobility.
